service: Foot evaluation and treatment for diabetic sensory neuropathy with loss of protective sensation (LOPS)
vignette: 71-year-old man with type 2 diabetes (ICD-10-CM E11.42) and diabetic peripheral neuropathy. Testing with the 5.07 Semmes-Weinstein monofilament at five plantar sites per foot, in random order and avoiding callused areas, shows absent sensation at 2 of 5 sites on the left foot and 1 of 5 on the right, documented in the note. His last foot evaluation for diabetic neuropathy with LOPS was 7 months ago, and he has not seen a podiatrist or other foot care specialist since. Today's visit documents a patient history and a physical examination with visual inspection of the forefoot, hindfoot and toe web spaces, evaluation of protective sensation, foot structure and biomechanics, vascular status and skin integrity, evaluation of the need for special footwear, and patient education. Debridement of plantar calluses and trimming of thickened nails are performed.
rationale_note: Boundary: absent sensation at exactly 2 of 5 sites on one foot; last LOPS exam 7 months ago; no interim foot specialist visit.
